findings.title: Refactored Run/backup dispatch path unexecuted without live credentials
findings.suggested_fix: Add an offline Run()-level test next to TestGithubRepositoryBackupWithMockAPI in internal/github_mock_test.go that reuses newGitFixtureServer and newGitHubMockAPI: back up/restore the environment (backupEnvironmentVariables/restoreEnvironmentVariables), call unsetEnvVarsExcept([]string{envPath}), explicitly unset GIT_BACKUP_INTERVAL and GIT_BACKUP_CRON (TestGetBackupInterval leaves GIT_BACKUP_INTERVAL set, and a non-zero value would block in waitForShutdown) plus the notification variables, then set GIT_BACKUP_DIR=t.TempDir(), GITHUB_TOKEN=mock-token, GITHUB_APIURL=<mock api URL>; call Run() and assert NoError, exactly one bundle under <backupDir>/github.com/mockuser/<name> for each repo, and that <backupDir>/.working has been removed. Assumption: GitHub() keeps honouring GITHUB_APIURL (internal/github.go:33), which the scratch prototype confirmed.
findings.why_it_matters: A green test run says nothing about the largest part of this refactor unless provider credentials are present: every test that drives Run() to success skips without a live token, so the new collectProviderBackupResults, createWorkingDir, scheduleBackups and runProviderBackups code is never executed (0% statement coverage at the reviewed head). A wrong env-var/provider pairing in the new dispatch table, a dropped working-directory step, or an early return in Run would ship with the suite passing. The repo already owns offline fixtures (newGitFixtureServer/newGitHubMockAPI) but TestGithubRepositoryBackupWithMockAPI calls githosts directly and bypasses Run(); routing a sibling test through Run() covers the refactored one-shot path deterministically, and a prototype of exactly that passed offline in about 5s in a scratch copy.
evidence: internal/github_mock_test.go:138 -- result := githubHost.Backup()  (the only deterministic backup test calls githosts directly; it never enters Run(), runProviderBackups or GitHub())

Coverage of the reviewed head (scratch copy of 136a4850, `go test ./internal/ -count=1 -coverprofile`, no credentials): collectProviderBackupResults 0.0%, runProviderBackups 0.0%, createWorkingDir 0.0%, scheduleBackups 0.0%, runScheduledJob 0.0%, execProviderBackups 0.0%, validateStartupConfig 46.7% (success return at backup.go:470 uncovered), Run 64.3% (backup.go:417-421 uncovered)

internal/backup_test.go:552-553 -- if os.Getenv(envGitLabToken) == "" { t.Skipf(...) }  (same guard pattern on every test that reaches a successful Run(); the only Run() calls that execute offline are the two early-error tests at backup_test.go:243 and :819)

Scratch prototype (TestScratchRunOneShotWithMockGitHub: Run() against the existing mock GraphQL API and git fixture server) passed offline and raised collectProviderBackupResults to 87.5%, createWorkingDir to 85.7%, runProviderBackups to 72.7%, scheduleBackups to 58.3%
No workflow under .github/workflows runs `go test` (grep count 0); the Makefile `test` target is the only runner, so there is no credentialed CI run compensating for the skips

findings.title: Extracted createWorkingDir duplicates existing resolveWorkingDir helper
findings.suggested_fix: In createWorkingDir (internal/backup.go:473-478) replace the four-line os.Getenv/if/filepath.Join block and its comment with `workingDIR := resolveWorkingDir(backupDIR)`; keep the log line and MkdirAll unchanged. Output is identical for every input, so the log line and created path do not change.
findings.why_it_matters: The directory that startup creates and the directory each backup run later deletes with os.RemoveAll are computed by two separate copies of the same GIT_WORKING_DIR-or-default rule, so a future change to one copy (trimming, GetEnvOrFile support, a different default name) silently makes soba create one path and clean up another. This refactor lifts the inline copy out of Run() into a new named helper, createWorkingDir, but keeps the copy instead of calling resolveWorkingDir(backupDir), which already lives in the same file and is what runProviderBackups uses. Calling it is a behaviour-identical one-line substitution (both return the env value when non-empty, else filepath.Join(backupDir, workingDIRName)) and leaves a single definition of the rule.
evidence: internal/backup.go:52,57 -- workingDir := resolveWorkingDir(backupDir) ... defer cleanupWorkingDir(workingDir, backupDir)  (the cleanup side uses the canonical helper; the create side does not)

provenance: function wrapper createWorkingDir is new in 136a4850 (line 473); the wrapped body lines 474-478 date from 476ed841 and resolveWorkingDir from 6adadb6b (Jon Hadfield 2026-06-24), i.e. the duplication pre-dates this change and the refactor re-housed it in a new helper rather than removing it

residual_risks.text: The PR's "log output unchanged" claim holds except for two narrow, log-only differences, both verified against base c77f548; neither changes which providers run or what is backed up, and neither needs a fix. (1) internal/backup.go:101 `bitbucketAPITokenDefined() || bitbucketOAuthDefined()` short-circuits, where the base read all five BitBucket variables on every backup run. With complete BitBucket API-token credentials plus a BITBUCKET_USER_FILE, BITBUCKET_KEY_FILE or BITBUCKET_SECRET_FILE that points at an unreadable file, GetEnvOrFile's `file ... does not exist` / `error opening file` line (internal/envfile.go:35-39) is now logged once per backup run (from Bitbucket(), internal/bitbucket.go:19-21) instead of twice; it still appears at startup via checkProvidersDefined. (2) internal/backup.go:219 logs the BitBucket compare method through the shared strings.EqualFold check where the base used strings.ToLower(compare) == "refs", so a BITBUCKET_COMPARE value that matches only under Unicode simple folding (for example "ref" + U+017F) is now logged as `refs` instead of `clone`; ASCII values are unaffected.
residual_risks.basis: (1) established by reading, not executed; (2) observed in the adversarial reviewer's randomized differential run (40,000 environment configurations, base vs head) as the only output difference

residual_risks.text: Two restructured runtime paths were verified by reading only, because they need provider credentials or block on a signal: the scheduled path (GIT_BACKUP_INTERVAL / GIT_BACKUP_CRON -> scheduleBackups -> runScheduledJob, internal/backup.go:491-541) and the non-GitHub entries of the provider dispatch in collectProviderBackupResults (internal/backup.go:97-123). By inspection the provider order (BitBucket, Gitea, GitHub, GitLab, Azure DevOps, Sourcehut) and predicates match the base, runScheduledJob assigns the package-level `job` without shadowing, and the job options keep their original order. The rewritten assertion helpers of TestGiteaOrgsRepositoryBackup (assertGiteaOrgTwoOnlyBackedUp, assertGiteaAllOrgsBackedUp, dirHasEntryWithPrefix) compiled but never ran, since that test skips without Gitea credentials; their equivalence to the removed inline assertions also rests on reading.
residual_risks.basis: reviewer inspection; `go test ./internal/ -count=1` at the reviewed head skips every credentialed test

testing_gaps.text: Startup configuration log output: no repository test asserts any line written by displayStartupConfig or its new label-parameterised helpers (logProviderOrgs, logProviderBackupsToKeep, logProviderCompareMethod, logProviderBackupLFS; internal/backup.go:188-300), including the deliberately preserved `Gitlab backup LFS` and `Organistations` spellings. Equivalence with the base was shown only out of tree, by the reviewers' scratch differential runs (byte-identical output over 6,000 to 40,000 random environments). A table test that swaps the package-level `logger` for a buffer and sets provider variables with t.Setenv would pin the PR's "log output unchanged" contract.

Scheduled mode: no test drives Run() with GIT_BACKUP_INTERVAL or GIT_BACKUP_CRON, so the interval and cron branches of scheduleBackups (internal/backup.go:501-515) and runScheduledJob (internal/backup.go:525-541) never execute. Nothing verifies that the package-level `job` is still assigned through the new helper, which execProviderBackups (internal/backup.go:35) relies on to avoid os.Exit(1) after a failed backup in daemon mode and runProviderBackups (internal/backup.go:87) uses for the next-run banner.

Provider credential validation: the error branches moved into checkJustTokenProvider (blank token, internal/backup.go:357-359) and checkUserAndPasswordProvider (partially configured provider, internal/backup.go:381-386) are not executed by the suite; only the `no providers defined` outcome is asserted (internal/backup_test.go:787-801).

Notification titles: the new backupStatusTitle switch (internal/notify.go:31-39), which now supplies the title for the Telegram, ntfy and Slack messages (notify.go:104, 191, 216), has no test and no test file references it. There is no current regression: the three title literals are byte-identical to the base and the switch matches the three removed copies. A four-row table test (for example TestBackupStatusTitle in a new internal/notify_test.go) asserting (1,0) -> succeeded, (3,2) -> completed with errors, (0,2) -> failed and (0,0) -> failed against literal strings would pin it.

demoted_findings.title: New backupStatusTitle switch has no test
demoted_findings.suggested_fix: Add a table-driven test (e.g. TestBackupStatusTitle in a new internal/notify_test.go) asserting backupStatusTitle(1,0)==titleBackupsSucceeded text, (3,2)==the 'completed with errors' text, (0,2)==the 'failed' text and (0,0)==the 'failed' text, comparing against literal expected strings rather than the title constants so the test does not mirror the code under test. An equivalent prototype passed in a scratch copy.
demoted_findings.first_evidence: internal/notify.go:31 -- func backupStatusTitle(succeeded, failed int) string {
demoted_findings.why_it_matters: The headline of every Slack, ntfy and Telegram notification now comes from one new three-branch function that no test executes, so a reordered or mis-edited case (for example a total failure reported under the 'succeeded' title, or the zero-succeeded/zero-failed case falling into the wrong branch) would reach all three channels at once with the suite green. Before this change the three copies could only drift individually; now a single untested switch owns the contract. It is a pure function of two ints, so a four-row table test pins it completely.
evidence: internal/notify.go:31 -- func backupStatusTitle(succeeded, failed int) string {
Coverage of the reviewed head (scratch copy, no credentials): internal/notify.go:31 backupStatusTitle 0.0%; all four blocks notify.go:31-38 have hit count 0
Text search of internal/*_test.go for backupStatusTitle, titleBackups and 'soba backups' returns no matches; callers are notify.go:104 (Telegram), :191 (ntfy Title header), :216 (Slack)

Byte comparison of the three title literals between base c77f548 and head 136a485 (including the leading U+FE0F variation selectors) shows them identical, so there is no current regression; the gap is the missing guard
demoted_findings.demotion_reason: Testing-only absence-of-coverage P3 from a single reviewer, with no violated contract and no current defect: the reviewer's own evidence shows the titles and the switch are byte-identical to the base. A missing test for a three-branch pure function is not material enough to be the primary coverage finding for internal/notify.go; the concrete test is kept as a testing gap.

per_finding.2: Kept primary. The duplicated lines predate this change, but the change created the new helper that houses the copy, so it is not routed as pre-existing. Concrete maintenance benefit, no runtime defect: P3 stands.
